title: 1971 Oklahoma Wishbone Set NCAA Rushing Record: 472.4 Yards a Game
question: What NCAA rushing record did Oklahoma's 1971 wishbone offense set?
answer: The 1971 Sooners averaged 472.4 rushing yards per game, 5,196 yards in 11 regular-season games, an NCAA record. Barry Switzer ran the wishbone as offensive coordinator for head coach Chuck Fairbanks.
summary: Oklahoma's 1971 wishbone ran for 472.4 yards a game, an NCAA record. Meet the Sooners offense led by Jack Mildren and Greg Pruitt under Fairbanks and Switzer.
body: If you want one number that explains why the wishbone became part of Oklahoma's identity, start with 472.4. That is how many rushing yards per game the 1971 Sooners averaged across 11 regular-season games, 5,196 yards in all, which set an NCAA record. Only regular-season games counted toward official NCAA records then, so the bowl game isn't part of the figure.

Chuck Fairbanks was the head coach, and his offensive coordinator was a young assistant named Barry Switzer. The Sooners led the nation in scoring at roughly 45 points per game and set an NCAA record for total offense. They also set school records with 62 rushing touchdowns and better than seven yards per carry.

Quarterback Jack Mildren was the engine. He ran for 1,140 yards, an NCAA rushing record for a quarterback at the time, and he was named an All-American and an Academic All-American. Halfback Greg Pruitt was a consensus All-American and finished third in the Heisman voting.

The only blemish on the season was the 35-31 Game of the Century loss to No. 1 Nebraska. Oklahoma closed with a 40-22 win over Auburn in the Sugar Bowl on Jan. 1, 1972. Mildren ran for 149 yards and three touchdowns in that game and was named its most outstanding player. The Sooners finished 11-1 and No. 2 in the final AP poll.
Two seasons later Switzer became head coach, and the wishbone powered OU to national titles in 1974, 1975 and 1985.
